gaps.sentence: ___ the weather improves, the crossing will be cancelled.
gaps.explanation: Unless = if the weather doesn't improve — matching the cancellation.

gaps.sentence: Cut the onions, fry them gently and ___, stir in the cream.
gaps.hint: the last step of a sequence
gaps.explanation: 'Finally' closes a list of actions; 'firstly' opens one, while 'initially'/'at first' contrast with later events.

gaps.sentence: She speaks fluent Mandarin; ___, she reads classical Chinese.
gaps.explanation: 'Moreover' adds a further, even more remarkable achievement.

gaps.sentence: He was warned repeatedly; ___, he ignored every safety rule.
gaps.explanation: He ignored the warnings despite receiving them: nevertheless marks that contrast.

gaps.sentence: She is not only a gifted violinist ___ a composer of some note.
gaps.explanation: 'Not only A but also B' joins the two parallel noun phrases.

gaps.sentence: He had hardly stepped off the plane ___ he was rushed into a meeting.
The essay was submitted late and, ___, it ignored the brief entirely.
gaps.explanation: 'What is more' adds a further, stronger point to an already negative picture.

gaps.sentence: ___ she was utterly exhausted, she stayed to help clear up.
gaps.explanation: 'Even though' concedes a known fact: she was exhausted and still stayed.
